verdict.rationale: The skills CLI has no natural-language interface of its own; it uses structured subcommands and flags (add, find, update, remove, init). It is, however, built to be driven by coding agents. A runtime probe showed it detects when an agent is running it and switches to promptless mode, and it offers non-interactive flags and `skills use` piping or `--agent` launch into Claude Code and others. A user can therefore operate it in natural language only indirectly, by telling their agent what to do. Missing for 10: a native natural-language command or intent interface, first-party docs on operating the product via natural-language prompts, and independent hands-on corroboration of natural-language-driven workflows.
